articles.title: Central Asia Metals PLC's Dividend Analysis
articles.summary: Central Asia Metals PLC (CAMLF) recently announced a total dividend of $0.11 per share, with the ex-dividend date set for 2026-09-24. This includes a $0.11 per share cash dividend payable on 2026-10-22. For value investors, the ex-dividend date matters because shareholders must own the stock before that date to qualify for the payment, while the paydate marks when the cash actually arrives.

articles.title: Central Asia Metals CEO: 'Really positive' H1 as Cygnus deal and drill assays loom
articles.summary: Central Asia Metals PLC (AIM:CAML, OTC:CAMLF) CEO Gavin Ferrar spoke with Proactive's Stephen Gunnion about the company's strong first-half 2026 performance, the proposed acquisition of Cygnus Metals, and exploration programmes that could drive further news flow this year. Ferrar described a "really positive first six months of the year, both operationally and financially," helped by record copper prices, strong zinc prices and solid operational performance. Group revenue rose 46% to $145.5 million year-on-year, EBITDA climbed almost 90% to $75.5 million, and profit before tax reached $59.3 million. The company generated almost $47 million of cash in H1 and declared an 8p dividend - 40% of free cash flow, within its 30-50% policy - ending the period with $97.2 million of cash. Ferrar discussed the proposed Cygnus Metals acquisition, agreed at an equity value of A$232 million payable in CAML shares, which would add copper exposure in a tier-one jurisdiction alongside an existing resource, infrastructure and exploration potential. Cygnus shareholders vote on 18 September, with CAML targeting ownership in early October if the deal proceeds. Exploration could provide further catalysts, with maiden drilling assays expected in the coming weeks and more drilling planned: "We're all waiting on tenterhooks for the assays to come out," Ferrar said. Central Asia Metals remains on track for its 2026 copper, zinc and lead production guidance as it looks to benefit from elevated commodity prices. articles.title: Faron Pharmaceuticals, Central Asia Metals, Gelion, S&U, Mila Resources, Georgina Energy
articles.summary: Faron Pharmaceuticals Limited (AIM:FARN) is set to start its phase IIb BEXERA trial for blood cancer drug bexmarilimab in the second half of this year. It'll test the drug in 90 patients across the US, Europe and the UK, funded by a €40 million rights issue. Central Asia Metals PLC (AIM:CAML, OTC:CAMLF) has nearly doubled first-half earnings on higher copper and zinc prices plus higher output. Profit before tax jumped 203%, and the interim dividend's been lifted to 8p. Gelion PLC (AIM:GELN, OTC:GELNF, FRA:X0S) has completed drone testing with QinetiQ on its sulfur battery cathode material. Cells handled repeated high-power take-off and landing cycles with barely any performance loss. S&U PLC (LSE:SUS) has hit record capital receivables of £616 million for its first half, up 20% on last year. Growth's been led by its motor finance arm Advantage, where deal numbers jumped 50%. Mila Resources PLC (LSE:MILA) has roughly doubled the gold resource at its Coffey deposit in Western Australia. It's now sitting at 41,300 ounces, with the company saying the system could extend well beyond the current resource. Georgina Energy PLC (LSE:GEX) has completed a £1.25 million fundraise to advance its Mount Winter project. Investors also get a warrant for every share, exercisable at 14p over the next five years.
